# AutoEP: fused Triton kernel for the clamped expert activations

<!-- r3 2026-10-15: branch peng-add-fuse-fn-clamped-form-v2 (worktree /fsx/peng/workspace/ds-add-fuse-fn-clamped-form-v2)
on master 5f266e26d; pushed to the PR's branch peng-add-fuse-fn-clamped-form-v1 with --force-with-lease (GitHub
shows the PR's commit 90c9660dd in conflict with master). DRAFT 2026-10-12, for the PR body of #8652. Replaces the whole current body. Items marked TODO(user) need the
submitter. Job IDs of every result: SOURCES.md. -->

**Branch:** `peng-add-fuse-fn-clamped-form-v1`, rebased on `master` at `5f266e26d` (2026-10-15). The expert activation registry it
registers into is merged (#8650), and so is the fused gate+up projection (#8733), which this PR now also covers.
**Part of:** #8672 (Q4 2026 roadmap), "Mixture-of-Expert (MoE) Training Scaling and Kernel Development": "AutoEP
Performance Optimization & Parallel Folding (AutoEP + AutoTP)" (PoC @tohtana @pengdurice). Follows the merged expert
activation registry (#8650) and MiniMax-M3 preset (#8651).

## Summary

The clamped expert activations `swiglu_clamped` (DeepSeek-V4) and `swiglu_oai` (GPT-OSS, MiniMax-M3) run as plain
PyTorch expressions that keep about four `[rows, ffn]` temporaries for backward. Plain `swiglu` has fused Triton
kernels that keep only `gate` and `up`. This PR adds the same kernels for the clamped forms, for both expert layouts:

- `gate_up_impl="separate"` (two grouped GEMMs): `swiglu_clamped(gate, up, ...)`.
- `gate_up_impl="fused"` (one grouped GEMM, #8733): `swiglu_clamped_packed(gate_up, ...)`, which reads the two halves
  of the packed GEMM output in place, as master's `swiglu_packed` does.

At the busiest rank of a MiniMax-M3 run that ran out of memory (1,045,081 rows x 3,072, bf16), one `swiglu_oai`
call goes from 41.86 GiB extra peak memory and 77.8 ms to 17.94 GiB and 11.9 ms, the same as plain `swiglu`.

## Duplicate check

Open PRs and issues searched on 2026-10-12 for "swiglu", "clamp", "expert activation" and "gpt-oss": no other work on
fused clamped activations. #8748 (another author, open) adds a different kernel, `swiglu_weighted` (routing weight
inside the activation, plain `swiglu` only), to the same two files (`swiglu_triton.py` and the registry in
`ep_experts.py`). The two do not overlap in function; whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

## Problem

Each clamped form is two clamps, a sigmoid, three products and an add in plain PyTorch, each a full `[rows, ffn]`
temporary, most of them saved for backward. On an expert-parallel rank this is where the memory goes, because
AutoEP has no capacity limit and real routers send some ranks several times the mean number of rows.

MiniMax-M3 at 65,536 tokens with expert parallel 32 on 4 nodes of 8 H200 ran out of memory there: the busiest rank
received 1,045,081 rows (3.99 times its own 262,144) and failed inside `apply_expert_activation` on one 11.96 GiB
temporary, with 129.50 GiB already in use. (Setup: all 60 layers, real checkpoint, `minimax_m3` preset, ZeRO-3 with
the optimizer state on the host, activation checkpointing; torch 2.8.0+cu126, transformers 5.15.1, DeepSpeed master
`4a5856c25` plus the then-open registry PR.) Over the 57 MoE layers, the busiest of 32 ranks received a median 4.20
times the mean number of rows (maximum 7.84).

## The change

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `deepspeed/ops/triton_ops/swiglu_triton.py` | `_swiglu_clamped_fwd_kernel` / `_swiglu_clamped_bwd_kernel`, modelled on master's swiglu kernels: int64 offsets, float32 math, one rounding on store, `OAI: tl.constexpr` selects the form, `PACKED: tl.constexpr` reads `gate` and `up` from one `[rows, 2 * INTER]` tensor with master's packed indexing. The clamp gradient passes at the limit, as `torch.clamp`'s does. Public `swiglu_clamped(gate, up, alpha, limit, oai)` and `swiglu_clamped_packed(gate_up, alpha, limit, oai)`; plain-PyTorch fallback without Triton or on the CPU. The packed backward raises for `create_graph=True`, as master's packed swiglu does |
| `deepspeed/moe/ep_experts.py` | registers the kernels as `fused_fn` and `packed_fused_fn` of `swiglu_clamped` and `swiglu_oai`. Nothing else changes: the grouped-GEMM expert paths reach them through `apply_expert_activation(..., fused=True)` and `apply_packed_expert_activation`; the for-loop reference path keeps `fused=False` |
| `docs/_pages/config-json.md` | one sentence: which forms run a fused kernel |
| `tests/unit/v1/ops/triton_ops/test_swiglu_triton.py`, `tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_expert_activation.py` | see Tests |

Size: 264 added and 2 removed lines under `deepspeed/` (232 added in `swiglu_triton.py`, 32 in `ep_experts.py`).

## Measured

One H200, torch 2.8.0+cu126, Triton 3.4.0, through `apply_expert_activation` / `apply_packed_expert_activation`
(`fused=True`). 1,045,081 rows x 3,072 in bf16 (one `[rows, ffn]` tensor = 5.98 GiB), alpha 1.702, limit
7.0, inputs at 6 x standard normal so most values are past a clamp. Extra peak = `max_memory_allocated` during
forward + backward minus the memory allocated before (inputs and upstream gradient). Kept = memory still allocated
after the forward, minus the output. Time = median of 5 forward + backward passes after 3 warm-ups.

| Form | Layout | master `1c862f7df`: extra peak / kept / time | this PR: extra peak / kept / time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `swiglu` (existing kernels, for comparison) | separate | 17.94 GiB / 0.00 GiB / 11.9 ms | 17.94 GiB / 0.00 GiB / 11.9 ms |
| `swiglu` | packed | 17.94 / 0.00 / 11.9 ms | 17.94 / 0.00 / 11.9 ms |
| `swiglu_clamped` | separate | 35.88 / 17.94 / 51.6 ms | **17.94 / 0.00 / 11.9 ms** |
| `swiglu_clamped` | packed | 35.88 / 17.94 / 92.1 ms | **17.94 / 0.00 / 13.1 ms** |
| `swiglu_oai` | separate | 41.86 / 23.92 / 77.8 ms | **17.94 / 0.00 / 11.9 ms** |
| `swiglu_oai` | packed | 41.86 / 23.92 / 118.3 ms | **17.94 / 0.00 / 13.2 ms** |

Per MoE layer on that rank, `swiglu_oai` keeps 23.92 GiB less for backward and runs 6.5 times faster (separate) or
9.0 times faster (packed). The packed clamped kernels are 1.2-1.3 ms slower than master's packed `swiglu` kernel,
which does less arithmetic per element. Bench script: `expert_activation_bench.py` (TODO(user): attach as a gist or
drop this line).

## Tests

Command, from `tests/`, on 1 node of 8 H200 (143,771 MiB each, driver 580.126.09), torch 2.8.0+cu126, Triton 3.4.0,
transformers 5.15.1, pytest 9.1.1:

```bash
DEEPSPEED_RUN_H100_TESTS=1 python -m pytest unit/v1/ops/triton_ops/test_swiglu_triton.py \
    unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_expert_activation.py -v \
    -k "not (skewed_and_empty or accumulated_updates_and_checkpoint)"
```

Result: **204 passed**, 12 deselected, in 31 s. On master `5f266e26d` (2026-10-15): **204 passed**, 12 deselected, in 34 s on torch 2.8.0; the two empty-expert tests from #8733 on torch 2.9.1: 12 passed on this branch and 12 passed on master.

The two deselected tests are master's (#8733). On torch 2.8.0+cu126 on H200 they do not finish, on master as well
as on this branch: they pass an empty expert group (`counts = [37, 0, 291, 72]` and `[16, 0, 32, 16]`) to
`torch._grouped_mm`, whose backward never returns for some shapes when a group is empty on that torch version (GPU at
100% with no progress; known from MiniMax-M3 work, one-GPU reproduction available). AutoEP itself never passes an
empty group, because `generate_permute_indices` gives every local expert at least 8 rows. On torch 2.8.0 master's
`test_matches_separate_with_skewed_and_empty_experts[swiglu]` did not finish in 300 s; on torch 2.9.1+cu128 (Triton
3.5.1) both tests pass, **12 passed** on this branch and 12 passed on master.

New and changed tests:

| Test | What it would catch |
|---|---|
| `test_clamped_forward_matches_reference` (2 forms x 3 dtypes x 6 shapes) | a wrong output: compared with the expression evaluated in float32 and rounded once; inputs at scale 4 so about 8% are past a clamp; the kernel must also be no farther from float32 than the eager low-precision evaluation |
| `test_clamped_backward_matches_reference` (2 x 3 x 5) | wrong input gradients, the same way, with a random upstream gradient |
| `test_clamped_alpha_and_limit_are_honoured` | alpha or limit ignored; a nonzero gradient where an input was clamped |
| `test_clamped_gradient_at_the_limit_is_inclusive` | a gradient that stops at `gate == limit` or `up == -limit`, where `torch.clamp`'s passes |
| `test_clamped_empty_input`, `test_clamped_non_contiguous_input`, `test_clamped_shape_and_dtype_mismatch_rejected` | the edge cases master's swiglu tests cover |
| `test_clamped_packed_matches_the_separate_kernel_exactly` (2 forms x 2 dtypes x 4 shapes, including 3-D and empty) | a packed path that reads the wrong half or row: output and gradient bit-equal to the separate kernel |
| `test_fused_kernel_matches_plain_pytorch` (every form with a `fused_fn`) | `apply_expert_activation(fused=True)` differing from the plain form evaluated in float32 and rounded once (bf16, 256 x 3,072) |
| `test_packed_kernels_are_registered` (was `test_only_swiglu_has_a_packed_kernel`) | the fused gate+up path silently running the clamped forms in plain PyTorch |
| `test_grouped_gemm_paths_match_the_for_loop`, `test_packed_activation_matches_the_separate_halves` (master's, now running the new kernels) | the grouped-GEMM paths differing from the for-loop reference path |

`pre-commit run --files` passes on every changed file.

## Compatibility

The change is an elementwise kernel behind AutoEP's existing activation registry; it does not depend on the ZeRO
stage, offload or parallel layout.

| | Validated | Not validated |
|---|---|---|
| Precision | float32, float16, bf16 (kernel tests); bf16 through the expert paths | |
| Expert layouts | `gate_up_impl` `"separate"` and `"fused"`; `torch._grouped_mm` and Triton grouped-GEMM paths (unit tests) | |
| End to end | | no training job has run with this kernel. The MiniMax-M3 runs on 4 nodes used the plain PyTorch form (the out-of-memory case above was avoided with expert parallel 4) |
| Accelerators | CUDA (H200); CPU fallback (plain PyTorch) | ROCm, XPU and other Triton backends. The packed path sets the device with `torch.cuda.device` (`#ignore-cuda`), as master's packed swiglu does |

## AI assistance

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -122,14 +122,44 @@ def _swiglu_oai(gate: torch.Tensor, up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float
     return (up + 1.0) * (gate * torch.sigmoid(gate * alpha))
 
 
+def _swiglu_clamped_fused(gate: torch.Tensor, up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops.swiglu_triton import swiglu_clamped
+    return swiglu_clamped(gate, up, alpha=alpha, limit=limit, oai=False)
+
+
+def _swiglu_oai_fused(gate: torch.Tensor, up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops.swiglu_triton import swiglu_clamped
+    return swiglu_clamped(gate, up, alpha=alpha, limit=limit, oai=True)
+
+
+def _swiglu_clamped_packed_fused(gate_up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops.swiglu_triton import swiglu_clamped_packed
+    return swiglu_clamped_packed(gate_up, alpha=alpha, limit=limit, oai=False)
+
+
+def _swiglu_oai_packed_fused(gate_up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float) -> torch.Tensor:
+    from deepspeed.ops.triton_ops.swiglu_triton import swiglu_clamped_packed
+    return swiglu_clamped_packed(gate_up, alpha=alpha, limit=limit, oai=True)
+
+
 register_expert_activation("swiglu",
                            _swiglu,
                            fused_fn=_swiglu_fused,
                            gate_fn=F.silu,
                            packed_fused_fn=_swiglu_packed_fused)
 register_expert_activation("geglu_tanh", _geglu_tanh, gate_fn=_gelu_tanh)
-register_expert_activation("swiglu_clamped", _swiglu_clamped, uses_limit=True, gate_fn=F.silu)
-register_expert_activation("swiglu_oai", _swiglu_oai, uses_alpha=True, uses_limit=True)
+register_expert_activation("swiglu_clamped",
+                           _swiglu_clamped,
+                           fused_fn=_swiglu_clamped_fused,
+                           uses_limit=True,
+                           gate_fn=F.silu,
+                           packed_fused_fn=_swiglu_clamped_packed_fused)
+register_expert_activation("swiglu_oai",
+                           _swiglu_oai,
+                           fused_fn=_swiglu_oai_fused,
+                           uses_alpha=True,
+                           uses_limit=True,
+                           packed_fused_fn=_swiglu_oai_packed_fused)
 
 
 def apply_expert_activation(gate: torch.Tensor,

@@ -250,3 +250,235 @@ def swiglu_packed(gate_up: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
         return _swiglu_eager(gate, up)
 
     return _SwiGLUPackedFn.apply(gate_up)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Clamped forms: silu(clamp(gate)) * clamp(up)            ("swiglu_clamped", DeepSeek-V4)
+#                (clamp(up) + 1) * g * sigmoid(alpha * g)  ("swiglu_oai", GPT-OSS / MiniMax-M3), g = clamp(gate)
+# gate is clamped from above only, up on both sides. Same fusion as above: one kernel each way, float32
+# math, only gate and up saved for backward. The eager expression saves about five [rows, ffn] temporaries
+# (the two clamps, the sigmoid, the products); on an expert-parallel rank that receives several times the
+# average rows this is where the memory goes (MiniMax-M3, 65,536 tokens: an 11.96 GiB temporary here).
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+if _TRITON_AVAILABLE:
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _swiglu_clamped_fwd_kernel(gate_ptr, up_ptr, out_ptr, n_elements, alpha, limit, OAI: tl.constexpr,
+                                   PACKED: tl.constexpr, INTER: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr):
+        pid = tl.program_id(axis=0).to(tl.int64)
+        offsets = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+        mask = offsets < n_elements
+        if PACKED:
+            # gate_ptr and up_ptr are the same [rows, 2 * INTER] tensor, as in _swiglu_packed_fwd_kernel.
+            gate_offsets = (offsets // INTER) * (2 * INTER) + offsets % INTER
+            up_offsets = gate_offsets + INTER
+        else:
+            gate_offsets = offsets
+            up_offsets = offsets
+
+        gate = tl.load(gate_ptr + gate_offsets, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+        up = tl.load(up_ptr + up_offsets, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+        g = tl.minimum(gate, limit)
+        u = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(up, -limit), limit)
+
+        if OAI:
+            out = (u + 1.0) * (g * tl.sigmoid(g * alpha))
+        else:
+            out = (g * tl.sigmoid(g)) * u
+
+        tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, out.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _swiglu_clamped_bwd_kernel(grad_out_ptr, gate_ptr, up_ptr, grad_gate_ptr, grad_up_ptr, n_elements, alpha,
+                                   limit, OAI: tl.constexpr, PACKED: tl.constexpr, INTER: tl.constexpr,
+                                   BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr):
+        pid = tl.program_id(axis=0).to(tl.int64)
+        offsets = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+        mask = offsets < n_elements
+        if PACKED:
+            gate_offsets = (offsets // INTER) * (2 * INTER) + offsets % INTER
+            up_offsets = gate_offsets + INTER
+        else:
+            gate_offsets = offsets
+            up_offsets = offsets
+
+        grad_out = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + offsets, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+        gate = tl.load(gate_ptr + gate_offsets, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+        up = tl.load(up_ptr + up_offsets, mask=mask).to(tl.float32)
+        g = tl.minimum(gate, limit)
+        u = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(up, -limit), limit)
+        # torch.clamp passes the gradient through where the input is inside the limits, inclusive.
+        pass_gate = gate <= limit
+        pass_up = (up >= -limit) & (up <= limit)
+
+        if OAI:
+            sig = tl.sigmoid(g * alpha)
+            f = g * sig
+            df = sig * (1.0 + alpha * g * (1.0 - sig))
+            grad_gate = grad_out * (u + 1.0) * df
+            grad_up = grad_out * f
+        else:
+            sig = tl.sigmoid(g)
+            f = g * sig
+            df = sig * (1.0 + g * (1.0 - sig))
+            grad_gate = grad_out * u * df
+            grad_up = grad_out * f
+        grad_gate = tl.where(pass_gate, grad_gate, 0.0)
+        grad_up = tl.where(pass_up, grad_up, 0.0)
+
+        tl.store(grad_gate_ptr + gate_offsets, grad_gate.to(grad_gate_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+        tl.store(grad_up_ptr + up_offsets, grad_up.to(grad_up_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask)
+
+    class _SwiGLUClampedFn(torch.autograd.Function):
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def forward(ctx, gate: torch.Tensor, up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float, oai: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+            gate = gate.contiguous()
+            up = up.contiguous()
+            out = torch.empty_like(gate)
+            n_elements = gate.numel()
+            if n_elements > 0:
+                grid = (triton.cdiv(n_elements, _BLOCK_SIZE), )
+                _swiglu_clamped_fwd_kernel[grid](gate,
+                                                 up,
+                                                 out,
+                                                 n_elements,
+                                                 float(alpha),
+                                                 float(limit),
+                                                 OAI=oai,
+                                                 PACKED=False,
+                                                 INTER=1,
+                                                 BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE,
+                                                 num_warps=_NUM_WARPS)
+            ctx.save_for_backward(gate, up)
+            ctx.alpha, ctx.limit, ctx.oai = float(alpha), float(limit), bool(oai)
+            return out
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def backward(ctx, grad_out: torch.Tensor):
+            gate, up = ctx.saved_tensors
+            grad_out = grad_out.contiguous()
+            grad_gate = torch.empty_like(gate)
+            grad_up = torch.empty_like(up)
+            n_elements = gate.numel()
+            if n_elements > 0:
+                grid = (triton.cdiv(n_elements, _BLOCK_SIZE), )
+                _swiglu_clamped_bwd_kernel[grid](grad_out,
+                                                 gate,
+                                                 up,
+                                                 grad_gate,
+                                                 grad_up,
+                                                 n_elements,
+                                                 ctx.alpha,
+                                                 ctx.limit,
+                                                 OAI=ctx.oai,
+                                                 PACKED=False,
+                                                 INTER=1,
+                                                 BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE,
+                                                 num_warps=_NUM_WARPS)
+            return grad_gate, grad_up, None, None, None
+
+    class _SwiGLUClampedPackedFn(torch.autograd.Function):
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def forward(ctx, gate_up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float, oai: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+            gate_up = gate_up.contiguous()
+            inter = gate_up.shape[-1] // 2
+            out = gate_up.new_empty(gate_up.shape[:-1] + (inter, ))
+            n_elements = out.numel()
+            if n_elements > 0:
+                grid = (triton.cdiv(n_elements, _BLOCK_SIZE), )
+                # Triton uses the current device and stream, which may differ from the input tensor's device.
+                with torch.cuda.device(gate_up.device):  #ignore-cuda
+                    _swiglu_clamped_fwd_kernel[grid](gate_up,
+                                                     gate_up,
+                                                     out,
+                                                     n_elements,
+                                                     float(alpha),
+                                                     float(limit),
+                                                     OAI=oai,
+                                                     PACKED=True,
+                                                     INTER=inter,
+                                                     BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE,
+                                                     num_warps=_NUM_WARPS)
+            ctx.save_for_backward(gate_up)
+            ctx.alpha, ctx.limit, ctx.oai = float(alpha), float(limit), bool(oai)
+            return out
+
+        @staticmethod
+        def backward(ctx, grad_out: torch.Tensor):
+            # The Triton backward has no autograd graph, so create_graph would silently lose the second derivative.
+            if torch.is_grad_enabled():
+                raise RuntimeError("The packed clamped SwiGLU kernel has no second derivative; "
+                                   "backward with create_graph=True is not supported")
+            gate_up, = ctx.saved_tensors
+            grad_out = grad_out.contiguous()
+            grad_gate_up = torch.empty_like(gate_up)
+            n_elements = grad_out.numel()
+            if n_elements > 0:
+                grid = (triton.cdiv(n_elements, _BLOCK_SIZE), )
+                with torch.cuda.device(gate_up.device):  #ignore-cuda
+                    _swiglu_clamped_bwd_kernel[grid](grad_out,
+                                                     gate_up,
+                                                     gate_up,
+                                                     grad_gate_up,
+                                                     grad_gate_up,
+                                                     n_elements,
+                                                     ctx.alpha,
+                                                     ctx.limit,
+                                                     OAI=ctx.oai,
+                                                     PACKED=True,
+                                                     INTER=gate_up.shape[-1] // 2,
+                                                     BLOCK_SIZE=_BLOCK_SIZE,
+                                                     num_warps=_NUM_WARPS)
+            return grad_gate_up, None, None, None
+
+
+def _swiglu_clamped_eager(gate: torch.Tensor, up: torch.Tensor, alpha: float, limit: float, oai: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Pure-PyTorch reference used as the non-Triton fallback."""
+    gate = gate.clamp(max=limit)
+    up = up.clamp(min=-limit, max=limit)
+    if oai:
+        return (up + 1.0) * (gate * torch.sigmoid(gate * alpha))
+    return F.silu(gate) * up
+
+
+def swiglu_clamped(gate: torch.Tensor,
+                   up: torch.Tensor,
+                   alpha: float = 1.702,
+                   limit: float = 7.0,
+                   oai: bool = True) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Fused clamped SwiGLU.
+
+    ``oai=True``: ``(clamp(up) + 1) * g * sigmoid(alpha * g)`` with ``g = clamp(gate, max=limit)`` and
+    ``up`` clamped to ``[-limit, limit]`` (GPT-OSS, MiniMax-M3). ``oai=False``: ``silu(g) * clamp(up)``
+    (DeepSeek-V4). Falls back to the eager expression when Triton is unavailable or the tensors are on
+    the CPU.
+    """
+    if gate.shape != up.shape:
+        raise ValueError(f"swiglu_clamped expects gate and up to have the same shape, got {tuple(gate.shape)} "
+                         f"and {tuple(up.shape)}")
+    if gate.dtype != up.dtype:
+        raise ValueError(f"swiglu_clamped expects gate and up to have the same dtype, got {gate.dtype} and {up.dtype}")
+    if not _TRITON_AVAILABLE or gate.device.type == "cpu":
+        return _swiglu_clamped_eager(gate, up, alpha, limit, oai)
+    return _SwiGLUClampedFn.apply(gate, up, alpha, limit, oai)
+
+
+def swiglu_clamped_packed(gate_up: torch.Tensor,
+                          alpha: float = 1.702,
+                          limit: float = 7.0,
+                          oai: bool = True) -> torch.Tensor:

+def _clamped_tol(dtype):
+    # about one ulp of the dtype at the output magnitude, plus a small absolute floor
+    if dtype == torch.float32:
+        return dict(atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5)
+    if dtype == torch.float16:
+        return dict(atol=1e-4, rtol=1.5e-3)
+    return dict(atol=1e-3, rtol=1.2e-2)  # bfloat16
+
+
+def _clamped_eager(gate, up, alpha, limit, oai):
+    """The two forms as the model code writes them (GptOssExperts / DeepseekV4Experts._apply_gate)."""
+    gate = gate.clamp(max=limit)
+    up = up.clamp(min=-limit, max=limit)
+    if oai:
+        return (up + 1.0) * (gate * torch.sigmoid(gate * alpha))
+    return F.silu(gate) * up
+

+def _clamped_reference(gate, up, alpha, limit, oai, grad_out=None):
+    """Eager expression in float32 on the same inputs, rounded once to the input dtype; optionally its
+    gradients (with grad_out also upcast), rounded the same way."""
+    g = gate.detach().float().requires_grad_(grad_out is not None)
+    u = up.detach().float().requires_grad_(grad_out is not None)
+    out = _clamped_eager(g, u, alpha, limit, oai)
+    if grad_out is None:
+        return out.to(gate.dtype)
+    out.backward(grad_out.float())
+    return out.detach().to(gate.dtype), g.grad.to(gate.dtype), u.grad.to(gate.dtype)
